notes: 2026-08-31 BATCH 2, direction 2 (PROJECT_SUMMARY 5.14). Built on arm0_ctl and differing from it in window_mode ONLY, so the batch-1 control is still the control and no new control run is needed. The window is [span_lo, span_hi] x the CANDIDATE's own transition, so 'walk S* out of the window' stops existing rather than being penalised -- the complement of arm2_brack, which penalises it on a fixed window. SHAPE QUESTION ONLY: this declares the dose scale a nuisance, which is legitimate for radialization and wrong for fitting real data. Compare ONLY through fit.compare_arms, which re-scores every endpoint under arm0's objective: an arm minimising a window that moves with the candidate has cost values that are not comparable to anything, INCLUDING to its own values at other points. ARM 6: the SAME relative window with the guard DISABLED (w_anchor=0), and the only field separating it from arm5. It exists because the guard is the load-bearing part and an unguarded relative window is predicted to be WORSE THAN THE CONTROL: measured on Aug-30 endpoints, seeds 7 and 15 score 0.345 and 0.273 against base's 0.481 with no type-1 side anywhere in six decades, i.e. the bare window pays for collapse. If arm6 does not collapse, the guard is unnecessary and should be dropped; if it does, arm5 minus arm6 is the guard's effect. A negative-control arm, deliberately. BEFORE SUBMITTING, RESOLVE THE DEAD-OSCILLATOR SETTING AGAINST BATCH 1. This arm inherits arm0_ctl's anti-dead-oscillator configuration: w_osc=0.2 and w_amp=1.0 -- present in EVERY batch-1 arm, and verified numerically rather than by inspection (amp_floor identical at 0.08765; the osc and amp terms agree with the absolute cost's own to 6e-12 on values of order 5-16, and fired at 7 of 8 probe points, so they are not dead code) -- with the aliveness ramp OFF (amp_lo=null). WHETHER THAT IS ENOUGH IS EXACTLY WHAT arm1_ramp IS MEASURING, and it had not reported when this file was written. The two failure modes are INDEPENDENT: this arm is the RUNAWAY solution, the direction-2 counterpart of arm2_brack's bracketing barrier, and it says nothing about dead oscillators -- the anchor-validity penalty (w_anchor) charges a missing type-1 side, an unreachable transition and a dead surface, none of which is a Floquet or amplitude verdict. Benchmarking the runaway fix while dying of the other problem would confound the result. SO: read arm1_ramp (and arm4_floor) first. If the ramp is what keeps orbits alive, set amp_lo=0.05 in BOTH arm5_relwin and arm6_relwin_raw -- and the control for batch 2 becomes arm1_ramp, not arm0_ctl, with arm5 still differing from it in window_mode alone. Same reasoning for lo_factor if arm4 turns out to be the one that matters. Change BOTH relwin arms together, or the arm5-minus-arm6 contrast stops isolating w_anchor. A non-attracting but healthy-looking cycle (Floquet mu) is caught by NEITHER batch: it is post-hoc only, in fit/stability.py and contract C1, and is not something this arm introduces.
